target_ref_note: Pinned to the tagged DVWA v1.10 release (digininja/DVWA, the canonical 'Damn Vulnerable Web Application'). PHP + MariaDB/MySQL, GPL-3.0. DVWA grades every module low/medium/high/impossible: the low/medium/high source files are deliberately vulnerable (POSITIVE fixtures); the impossible source file is the hardened, parameterized/escaped twin (NEGATIVE decoy). This gives a positive and a false-positive denominator from a SINGLE module. v1.10 is stable for fixture pinning; if you re-pin to the newer 'Vulnerable APIs' release (2025-01-29) re-verify file paths — the vulnerabilities/<module>/source/<level>.php layout has been stable across releases but the API modules added new directories.
notes: Match rule identical to expected-findings.json (see tests/e2e/assertions.py). DVWA's per-module graded sources make precision testing cheap: source/{low,medium,high}.php are the vulnerable twins; source/impossible.php is the safe twin that MUST NOT be flagged. Select with: scripts/run-e2e-test.sh --target dvwa.

schema_changelog.v3: see expected-findings.json — negative_expectations[] decoys + precision/recall scorer.

expectations.description: SQL injection — unparameterized query built from $_GET['id'] (string concatenation into mysqli_query).
expectations.rationale: Canonical DVWA SQLi: "SELECT first_name, last_name FROM users WHERE user_id = '$id'" with no parameterization. Blind variant (sqli_blind) is an alternate file.

expectations.description: Reflected XSS — $_GET['name'] echoed into the response without output encoding.
expectations.rationale: Reflected XSS: echo 'Hello ' . $_GET['name'] with no htmlspecialchars().

expectations.description: Stored XSS — message/name persisted to DB and rendered without encoding.
expectations.rationale: Soft: stored XSS requires tracing a persisted value across write (guestbook insert) and read (render) paths; single-shot auditors catch reflected (dvwa-02) but often miss the stored variant. CWE-79 same class.

expectations.description: OS command injection — $_REQUEST['ip'] concatenated into a shell ping command (shell_exec).
expectations.rationale: Canonical command injection: shell_exec('ping ' . $target) with no validation; medium.php blacklists only '&&' and ';' (still bypassable).

expectations.description: File inclusion (LFI/RFI) — $_GET['page'] passed to include() with no allow-list.
expectations.rationale: include($_GET['page']); — path traversal / remote file inclusion. CWE-98 is the precise PHP-remote-file-inclusion tag; CWE-22 path traversal accepted; CWE-73 external-control-of-filename also valid.

expectations.description: Unrestricted file upload — uploaded file moved into webroot with no type/content validation.
expectations.rationale: Soft: move_uploaded_file into the webroot enabling webshell upload; medium.php checks $_FILES type (client-controlled, bypassable). Requires file-upload deep dive (cat-08).

negative_expectations.description: SQLi 'impossible' level uses a prepared statement (PDO ->prepare / ->bindParam) — NOT injectable.
negative_expectations.rationale: DVWA's designed safe twin of dvwa-01: $data = $db->prepare('SELECT ... WHERE user_id = (:id) ...'); $data->bindParam(':id', ...). Flagging it as SQLi is the textbook false positive the graded levels exist to catch.

negative_expectations.description: Command-exec 'impossible' level validates the IP with explode()+is_numeric octet checks and uses stripslashes — input is constrained, not injectable.
negative_expectations.rationale: Safe twin of dvwa-04: the target is split on '.' and each octet checked with is_numeric before being reassembled, so no shell metacharacters survive. A finding here is an FP.

negative_expectations.description: Reflected-XSS 'impossible' level wraps output in htmlspecialchars() — correctly encoded.
negative_expectations.rationale: Safe twin of dvwa-02: htmlspecialchars($_GET['name']) before echo. Encoded output is not XSS.

gated_categories.token_scope: DVWA has no PAT/scope/OAuth-token system; session-cookie auth only. No token_scope ground truth.
gated_categories.mitm: DVWA makes no outbound TLS calls of note. No mitm fixture.
gated_categories.deployment: DVWA ships an intentionally weak config but the fixture does not assert a specific deployment finding (config drift across releases). Not a gated-off category — just unfixtured here.
gated_categories.llm: No LLM SDK in DVWA; cat-09 gated off. Absent phase-05-llm-*.jsonl is pass-via-skip.
gated_categories.agentic: No MCP/agent/tool-definition surface in DVWA; profile.mcp_agentic.detected=false → cat-agentic gated off. Absent phase-05-agentic-*.jsonl is a LEGITIMATE skip.

always_on_categories.supply_chain: Always-on. DVWA's PHP dependencies are sparse (mostly vendored), but cat-supply_chain still runs; no specific supply_chain fixture is asserted.
